docs.title: Introduction to SMIRK
docs.text:
Get SMIRK here or download it directly from within Blender by searching for it in the Extensions Tab in Preferences.

GET SMIRK HERE GET SMIRK HERE

docs.title: What is it?
docs.text:
SMIRK is a system designed to help with stylized facial features like mouths and openings in general. It can be used for eyes and more as well.

At its core it's a set of tools that allows the user to cut a hole into the mesh using a circular base. This can be an edge loop on a mouth mesh, a simple mesh ribbon or even Grease Pencil

Many might know this as the "Boolean Mouth" but SMIRK comes with a subset of methods to approach the cutting process to enable maximum flexibility and performance in a production environment.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
You can install directly within Blender, by searching for SMIRK inside the "Get Extensions" panel.

You can also manually install it by going to the Releases panel here on the right and downloading the newest Zip File. This can be drag and dropped into Blender to be installed.

docs.text: What SMIRK is made of

docs.title: What it isn't
docs.text:
• SMIRK is not an auto-rigger and does not generate any armatures to make facial features animatable. This might change in the future when the scope of this addon changes.
  • SMIRK does not generate entire facial features. It does come with some mesh generation like the Rim and Inner Area which might be expanded on in the future.
  • SMIRK cannot be exported to game engines as it makes use of Blender's shaders and Geometry Nodes. Though a similar approach could possibly be recreated in a game engine.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
• Setup your objects first. You'll need a surface object like a head and a cutter object like Grease Pencil object or a Mouth Mesh/Circular Mesh.
  • Open your Side Panel and select the SMIRK Panel.
  • Select your Surface Mesh and click on Setup Proxy to create a Proxy Mesh (used internally to avoid dependency cycles)
  • Click on Add Smirk Modifier and fill in the fields, choose your cutter object as the cutter
  • Go to the new Cutter Object Subpanel
  • Now depending on the type of Cutter (Object or Grease Pencil) you click on Add SMIRK Cutter Vertex Group/GP Layer
  • Click on Edit Cutter Object to edit the cutter (you can do this manually too of course but this operator does some helpful additional things)
  • For Vertex Groups, select an edge loop and add it to your Cutter Mask Vertex Group
  • For Grease Pencil, edit on the Cutter Mask Layer and either use the fill tool to create the cutter or draw them manually (Make sure to make the drawn strokes cyclic in edit mode)
  • Click Go to Surface Object to return to the Surface
  • The basic setup is done and the modifier can now be further tweaked

docs.title: Wasn't This Released Before?
docs.text:
The SMIRK addon is an extension to the Geometry Nodes toolset I made a year ago with the same name.

This addon wraps these Geometry Node tools into a Blender extension that helps set up and adjust the Freeform Facial Feature workflow easily.

docs.title: Freeform Facial Features
docs.text:
Also FFF for short is not a professionally coined term and simply an umbrella term I came up with for heavily stylized facial features that work independently from the head's topology.

The Term as well as the system is heavily inspired by Disney's Detached Facial Features but since SMIRK also makes use of pure "face carving" and other techniques independent of DFF's SDFs (Signed Distance Fields used to create transitions), I felt like a separate, more broad term was necessary.

docs.title: Surface Object
docs.text:
The Surface Object is the main object that SMIRK will operate on. It's where the Mask and subsequent hole gets generated. In most cases this will be the head of your character.

SMIRK comes with an arsenal of tools that will help setup FFF on your Surface Object.

docs.title: Mode
docs.text: Choose between two modes which toggle specific features Simple Simple is a simplified Version of the tool that works great with a mesh-based approach Complex Complex adds Cutter Rim and Inner Area and is best suited for a Grease Pencil approach

docs.title: Exclusion Mask
docs.text: The parts of the geometry that go into the first output

docs.title: Mask
docs.text: Name of the Vertex Group or GP Layer used to determine the Body opening

docs.title: UV Map
docs.text: UV Map to transfer from. Important to fix UVs that might get broken through certain options

docs.title: Object
docs.text: Object that drives the Smirk Boolean

docs.title: Collection
docs.text: Collection that drives the Smirk Boolean

docs.title: Separate Instances
docs.text: Instead of displaying all objects of the collection, only display one

docs.title: Object Index
docs.text: determines which Instance to display. Reads the collection top down

docs.title: Mode
docs.text: Algorithm used to create the Cutter Mask

docs.title: Grid Resolution
docs.text: Resolution of the Grid. Higher gives more accurate results

docs.title: Offset
docs.text: Offsets the Grid Fill, basically spinning it around. Might help with quality in some cases

docs.title: Quality
docs.text: Subdivides the Cutter Mesh before Shrinkwrapping it

docs.title: Projected Shrinkwrap
docs.text: Uses Projected Shrinkwrap in addition to Nearest Surface which should yield better results, especially around harsher angles

docs.title: Hardsurface Precision
docs.text: Uses Manifold Boolean to calculate a better mask for Sharp Edges. Both this and the Cutter Mesh need to be manifold. Optimal for Hardsurface Objects. Has a performance impact

docs.title: Shader Attribute
docs.text: Attribute for the Mask used in the Shader to control Transparency

docs.title: Resample
docs.text: Resample the curve that drives the Boolean Cutter topology to control the resolution

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: The resolution of the Boolean Cutter. When turned off it uses the resolution of the Cutter Object

docs.title: Iterations
docs.text: How often the mesh gets subdivided. Higher values increase accuratcy but also performance

docs.title: Radius
docs.text: Overall Radius where Tesselation happens

docs.title: Threshold
docs.text: Determines thickness where each subdivision iteration takes places

docs.title: Subdivide entire Cutter
docs.text: Subdivides the entire Cutter Area instead of just around the boundary. Can lead to more accurate results with Cutout Mesh at the cost of performance

docs.title: Threshold
docs.text: Determines when faces should be deleted. Higher values create a larger hole

docs.title: Mode
docs.text: Algorithm used to snap the created boundary edge to back the Cutter

docs.title: Snap to Cutter
docs.text: Snaps the Boundary Edge to the cutter

docs.title: Smooth Snapping
docs.text: Smooths the area around the snapped Boundary Edge to create a cleaner mesh

docs.title: Smooth Iterations
docs.text: Intensity of the smoothing. High Values slow down performance

docs.title: Turn off Shader Mask
docs.text: Turns the Shader Mask fully opaque to not interfere with the Cutout Mesh.

docs.title: Material
docs.text: Material should be identical to the head but using the Custom Normal attribute to drive the Normal

docs.title: Rim Type
docs.text: Algorithm used to create the Rim

docs.title: Loop Cuts
docs.text: Add Loop Cuts to the Rim

docs.title: Thickness
docs.text: Overall Thickness of the Rim

docs.title: Width
docs.text: Width of the Rim

docs.title: Height
docs.text: Height of the Rim

docs.title: Reduce Overlap
docs.text: Reduces mesh overlap around sharp corners but potentially creates uneven thickness

docs.title: Smooth Loft
docs.text: Blur the generated Lofting Curve to get a smoother result

docs.title: Shrinkwrap Offset
docs.text: Adjust how closely the Rim snaps to the Object

docs.title: Resample
docs.text: Resample the curve that drives the Cutter Rim topology to control the resolution

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: The resolution of the Rim opening. When turned off it uses the resolution of the Cutter Object

docs.title: Flip
docs.text: Flips the direction of the Rim. New dynamic algorithm should hopefully make this option obsolete

docs.title: Flip Vertex Group
docs.text: Vertex Group used to manually flip Curves. Use this to fix some inconsistencies. Can also flip manual Loft Curves

docs.title: Custom Normal Attribute
docs.text: Attribute you use to adjust the normals of the Mouth Rim Material. 4.5 allows normals to be transferred directly so this shouldn't be needed anymore

docs.title: Scale Inner Area
docs.text: Scale the opening of the Inner Area

docs.title: Offset
docs.text: Moves the Inner Area towards the inside of the mesh

docs.title: Smooth Opening
docs.text: Smooths the start of the Inner Area. Useful for very angular mouths and to reduce overlap

docs.title: Smooth Amount
docs.text: Mix between unsmoothed and smoothed curve

docs.title: Loop Cuts
docs.text: Add Loop Cuts to the Inner Area

docs.title: Extrude Depth
docs.text: Determines how far the Inner Area reaches into the object

docs.title: Backside Type
docs.text: Algorithm used to create the Backside of the Inner Area

docs.title: Grid Offset
docs.text: Rotates the generated Grid Backside

docs.title: Merge Backside
docs.text: Merges the Backside to a single point

docs.title: Triangulate Backside
docs.text: Triangulates the Backside. Might give decent results with the N-Gon Type

docs.title: Scale Backside
docs.text: Scales the Backside

docs.title: Flatten Backside
docs.text: Amount of mixing between the A and B inputs

docs.title: Smooth Amount
docs.text: Controls the smoothness of the Inner Area

docs.title: Expand Area
docs.text: Exapnds the Inner Area when smoothed

docs.title: Rotate Inner Area
docs.text: Rotate the angle at which the Inner Area gets extruded

docs.title: Simplify Curve
docs.text: Dissolves Points using an angle threshold. Allows for lower mesh density that still matches the cutout

docs.title: Material
docs.text: Material of the Inner Area

docs.title: Shade Smooth
docs.text: Shade the Inner Area smooth

docs.title: Blur Normals
docs.text: Blur the normals of the Inner Area

docs.title: Resample
docs.text: Resample the curve that drives the Inner Area topology to control the resolution

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: The resolution of the Inner Area opening. When turned off it uses the resolution of the Cutter Object
